text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer ranks the EQE 350 second with 612 of 800 points behind the BMW i5 eDrive40 (635), mainly on handling, braking, boot space and price. Reviewer measured 404 km range for the EQE 350 versus 383 km for the i5 eDrive40. Reviewer states the EQE charges at up to 170 kW (10-80 % in 32 min) versus 205 kW (30 min) for the i5, and uses slightly more energy on the economy loop. Reviewer finds the EQE's drive refined and responsive, but the i5 eDrive40 is faster in the acceleration tests and livelier. Reviewer describes the EQE as comfort-oriented and handy thanks to the optional rear-axle steering, but its steering needs getting used to, while the i5 is lighter, more playful and steers more precisely. Reviewer measured 33.2 m from 100 km/h with warm brakes for the EQE versus 32.3 m for the i5. Reviewer describes the EQE's optional air suspension (2,083 EUR) as very comfortable and smooth. Reviewer praises the EQE's bright, well-structured displays and menus and rates its voice control among the fastest. Reviewer describes the EQE interior as more opulent, with high-quality build. Reviewer states the EQE's front seats are narrower with less shoulder support and the seat adjustment gives no feedback, rating the i5 better here. Reviewer states the EQE offers more rear legroom than the i5, though slightly less rear headroom and width. Reviewer states the EQE's boot holds 430 l and payload is 475 kg, versus 490 l and 578 kg for the i5. Reviewer measured the EQE quieter than the i5: 61 dB(A) versus 63 dB(A) at 130 km/h. Reviewer notes the EQE test car cost over 10,000 euros more than the i5 test car (93,123 vs 82,680 EUR) and rates the BMW better on value.
